decision: In-game prop: a crashed helicopter for the roof of the Snow Fortress, generated from a reference image by TRELLIS.2. Built by scene_kit at 34 studs across with a bottom pivot, decimated to 9,000 triangles in one mesh. The verdict above says to tile rather than decimate, and that advice was overridden deliberately: it is calibrated on broad terrain the player walks across, where losing the silhouette is fatal, whereas this is a compact object seen from outside. Rendered at 9,000 it still reads unmistakably as a wreck -- fuselage, cabin openings, bent rotor, tail boom, skids and debris -- so one mesh beats eight parts here. meshoptimizer was tried first and stalled at 53,366 triangles: 175,634 open edges mean it will not collapse across the boundaries, which is exactly the case Blender's decimate covers. Textures arrived as 2048 WebP, which Roblox cannot read and which puts EXT_texture_webp in extensionsRequired; gltf_post now converts them to 1024 PNG. Seen in game the mesh read well but was pale grey-white on a white roof and vanished at any distance, so the base colour is tinted to charcoal in the pipeline (0.38, 0.36, 0.34 with lift 0.03, mean 118 -> 45) and the map paints a scorch patch under it. Tinting in the pipeline rather than the map because a MeshPart's Color does not affect an applied texture.
